import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 674

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/674](https://www.erdosproblems.com/674)
- [Ko40] Ko, Chao, *Note on the Diophantine equation $x^xy^y=z^z$*. J. Chinese Math. Soc.
  (1940), 31-39.
-/

namespace Erdos674

/-- The set of integer solutions to $x^x y^y = z^z$ with $x, y, z > 1$. -/
def solutionSet : Set (ℕ × ℕ × ℕ) :=
  {(x, y, z) | 1 < x ∧ 1 < y ∧ 1 < z ∧ x ^ x * y ^ y = z ^ z}

/--
Are there any integer solutions to $x^xy^y=z^z$ with $x,y,z>1$?

Ko [Ko40] proved there are none if $(x,y)=1$, but there are in fact infinitely many solutions in
general - for example, $x=2^{12}3^6$, $y = 2^83^8$, and $z = 2^{11}3^7$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos674.lean"]
theorem erdos_674 : answer(True) ↔ solutionSet.Nonempty := by
  sorry

/--
There are in fact infinitely many integer solutions to $x^xy^y=z^z$ with $x,y,z>1$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos674.lean"]
theorem erdos_674.variants.infinite : solutionSet.Infinite := by
  sorry

end Erdos674

review.notes: No mathematical misformalizations were found in solutionSet or either theorem. The source explicitly asks for solutions with x,y,z > 1, states infinitude, and records an affirmative Lean-verified answer. Scratch checks verified the answer polarity, exclusion of 0 and 1 in every coordinate, equivalence of natural-number and integer existence formulations, and membership of the displayed witness. Both linked external proofs compiled and their axiom reports contained only standard axioms, with no sorryAx. Ko's original full text was not obtained; its bibliographic details were independently confirmed by MathSciNet, and the historical assertion in the docstring agrees with the cited problem page.
